note: Control identifiers (DP-1, API-2, ...) are local labels for readability only. This catalog is NOT a claim of conformance to NIST 800-53, SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, or any published framework. It describes the controls a one-owner software service handling customer data through a third-party model API would be expected to hold, and exists to demonstrate evidence-to-control review against a real operating business rather than a synthetic corpus. Written before the evidence was indexed, from control practice rather than from the evidence text, so that a control can fail. Several controls here are expected to come back MISSING for a business with no employees and no premises; that is the intended result, not a defect. Keyword rule: a keyword is included only if its presence in any document means this control's topic is under discussion. Bare common-English and cross-domain single tokens were removed after inspecting matches, because three of them produced false positives on the first run: "secret" matched "instance ids are not secret", "visitor" matched a website visitor in a rate-limit comment, and "indemnity" matched an NDA clause the business reviews rather than its own limit of liability. A fourth keyword was removed after the stemmer was corrected: "backed up" matched the phrasal verb in "pick back up when you're ready", which is a parked project resuming, not a data backup. Widening recall makes common phrasal verbs dangerous as keywords. A fifth keyword was removed when the evidence owner added a new document: "badge" on PE-1 (physical entry) matched "no badge you can buy carries legal weight" in a web-accessibility policy, where a badge is a trust seal displayed on a site, not a card that opens a door. PE-1 went from MISSING to PARTIAL on a business with no premises, and the only thing that changed was that the owner published an unrelated SOP. That is the pattern in all five removals: the catalog was not re-read when the corpus grew, and a single cross-domain token is the failure every time. A keyword must be unusable outside this control's topic, not merely common inside it.

controls.title: Customer Data Flow Is Written Down
controls.description: The business can state where customer data goes, which systems hold it, and which copies leave the customer's browser.

requirements.name: Destinations for customer data are stated
Storage locations are stated, including the absence of storage

controls.title: Retention Schedule
controls.description: Each category of customer data has a stated retention period rather than being kept indefinitely by default.

requirements.name: A retention period is stated for correspondence
A retention period is stated for customer-supplied files

controls.title: Deletion On Request
controls.description: A customer can ask for their data to be deleted, and the business states a time limit and any records it is obliged to keep.

requirements.name: A deletion request route and time limit exist
Records exempt from deletion are identified

controls.title: Third Parties That Receive Customer Data Are Named
controls.description: Every external service that customer data reaches is identified to the customer, not described in the abstract.

requirements.name: The model provider is named
Onward sharing is addressed

controls.title: Customer Data Excluded From Model Training
controls.description: The business states whether customer inputs are used to train a model, and on what basis.

requirements.name: A training-exclusion statement exists
The basis for the claim is attributed, not asserted bare

controls.title: Cardholder Data Kept Out Of Scope
controls.description: Card details are handled by a payment processor and never entered into or stored by the business's own systems.

requirements.name: Card handling is delegated to a processor
Customers are told not to send card or credential data through unsecured channels

controls.title: Public Endpoint Origin Restriction
controls.description: An endpoint reachable from the internet accepts cross-origin calls only from an allowlist, and caches are keyed so an allow or deny decision cannot be served to the wrong caller.

requirements.name: An origin allowlist is enforced
Cache correctness for origin-dependent responses is addressed

controls.title: Abuse And Spend Limits On A Metered Endpoint
controls.description: An endpoint that costs money per request bounds how many requests it will serve, not only what one request may do, and the limit's weaknesses are written down.

requirements.name: A per-caller rate limit exists
A service-wide ceiling or spend cap exists

controls.title: Untrusted Input Screening
controls.description: Input arriving from the public is screened before it reaches a model or a tool, and the output is checked before it reaches a customer.

requirements.name: Input screening exists
Output is validated before it is shown

controls.title: Secrets Management
controls.description: Credentials are held outside source control, and the handling of a live key is stated.

requirements.name: Secrets are kept out of the repository
Key scope or rotation is addressed

controls.title: Change Management With Rollback
controls.description: A change to production is made against a written procedure in which every step states how to verify it and how to undo it.

requirements.name: A written cutover or deployment procedure exists
Every step has a stated rollback

controls.title: Defect Tracking And Disposition
controls.description: Defects found are recorded with what is wrong and what was decided, rather than fixed silently or forgotten.

requirements.name: A defect log exists
Entries carry a disposition

controls.title: Support Commitment And Human Escalation
controls.description: A customer is told how quickly they will get a reply and how to reach a person, and an automated agent has a route to hand off.

requirements.name: A response-time commitment is published
A human escalation path exists

controls.title: Security Awareness Training
controls.description: People who handle customer data receive periodic security awareness training, with a record of completion.

requirements.name: A training requirement is defined
Completion is recorded

controls.title: Physical Access Control
controls.description: Premises or facilities holding customer data or equipment restrict physical entry and log visitors.

requirements.name: Physical entry restriction is defined
Visitor handling is defined

controls.title: Backup And Recovery
controls.description: Data the business could not rebuild is backed up on a schedule, and a restore has actually been tested.

requirements.name: A backup schedule exists
A restore has been tested

controls.title: Dependency Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Third-party packages are checked for known vulnerabilities and updated on a stated cadence.

requirements.name: Dependencies are scanned for known vulnerabilities
A patching cadence is defined

controls.title: Insurance And Liability Position
controls.description: The business has decided its insurance position and states the limits of its liability to customers.

requirements.name: An insurance position is stated
Contractual limits of liability are stated

controls.title: Access Removal When People Leave
controls.description: When someone with access to customer data stops working with the business, their access is removed on a stated timeline.

requirements.name: An offboarding step for access removal is defined
Who holds access is recorded

controls.title: Published Accessibility Conformance Claim Is Complete
controls.description: Any published accessibility conformance claim carries the five components WCAG 2.2 section 5.3.1 requires, so a reader can tell what was claimed, for which pages, and on what the claim rests. Derived from the standard text, not from the evidence: the five requirements below are the five components 5.3.1 enumerates, in its order.

requirements.name: Date of the claim is stated
requirements.needs: A date pattern. Keyword matching cannot express "a date is present": the documents write a bolded label followed by the value ("Date. 21 September 2026"), and a bare "date" keyword would match most of the corpus. Anchor a future pattern on the label, not on a date format. Until then this requirement is not evaluated and the control cannot reach SATISFIED. Empty keywords is the whole mechanism: the limitation is derived from the missing matcher, so attaching one clears it and no stored flag survives to contradict the verdict.

requirements.name: Guidelines title, version and URI are given
Conformance level satisfied is named
Pages covered are described, including whether subdomains are included
Web content technologies relied upon are listed

controls.title: Automated Interaction And Work Composition Are Disclosed
controls.description: A customer interacting with an automated system is told so, and can find out who performs the work. Anchored to statute rather than to the evidence: EU AI Act Article 50(1) requires providers to ensure a person is informed they are interacting with an AI system unless that is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person, with Article 50(5) requiring the information in a clear and distinguishable manner at the latest at first interaction; California Business and Professions Code 17941(b) requires bot disclosure that is clear, conspicuous and reasonably designed to inform, and 17941(a) provides no liability where disclosure is made. FTC Act section 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)(1)) supports the composition requirement but supplies no checklist: its operative text declares unfair or deceptive acts unlawful and names no disclosure duty, so it gives a standard to be judged against and not requirements to be tested. Read from the statutory texts, not from any summary.

requirements.name: Automated interaction is disclosed as automated
keywords: you are talking to a bot

requirements.name: Whether work is performed by employees or by software is stated
Subcontracting or onward delegation of the work is addressed
Disclosure is made at first interaction rather than on request
requirements.needs: Evidence of WHEN and HOW a disclosure is shown to a user, which a document corpus cannot carry. AI Act Article 50(5) requires the information at the latest at the time of first interaction, and 17941(b) requires it be clear and conspicuous; both are properties of the running interface, not of a policy file. A sentence in an SOP is evidence the claim exists, never evidence a user saw it before typing. Satisfying this needs a different evidence type, a screenshot or an interface test, not a better keyword.
